brief: A single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it, with five drawers in it.

requirements.requirement: A single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it
requirements.evidence: One Hex base · North half (piece:0,0,0;half-n) at q0 r0 level 0 is the only base. No other bases, covers, caps or parts added. The full base was swapped for a half because drawers only attach to a half base's cut face. Mesh check reads clear.

Only one drawer fits: a drawer seats on a cut face and a single base offers one cut face (find_sockets returned one drawer site, s1, now drawer:0#0,0#cut). The other drawer styles (notch, bay) need neighbouring bases beside this one, which the brief rules out. Five drawers would need five bases beside it, which breaks the single-base requirement.

finish.summary: Built a single hex base (a north half-base, one cell) with one drawer on its cut face. The brief asked for five drawers, which the configurator cannot fit into one base alone: each base offers only one drawer site. I did not add neighbouring bases, since the brief forbids anything beside it. Outcome is a compromise: single base met, five drawers not met (one drawer built). Caps on the open faces were left off to keep nothing else added; the configurator notes three open cap faces. Getting five drawers would need four more bases beside this one, which the brief excludes.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
